newsitem.title: UK: HTV shares rise on United News bid hopes.
newsitem.headline: HTV shares rise on United News bid hopes.

text.p: Shares in HTV Plc rose in early trading Monday after a Mail on Sunday report said the company could be target of a bid from United News & Media, topping a bid from Carlton Communications Plc.
The stock was up 13p at 348-1/2 by 0707 GMT.
Speculation of further bids in the television sector has picked up ahead of law changes taking effect November 1 which will relax rules on media ownership.
London-based Carlton has long been rumoured as a likely bidder for HTV, which holds the terrestrial commercial TV franchise to broadcast to Wales and the West of England.
Yet some believe bidders may baulk at making offers for companies such as HTV whose share prices have already been inflated by takeover hopes.
HTV shares were trading at less than 140p at the start of 1995.
No-one at HTV was immediately available for comment, while a spokesman for United News said the company's policy was to not comment on speculation.
United News shares were down 5-1/2p at 690 by 0756 GMT and Carlton was down 3p at 483-1/2.
